simulator.strands_of_fate.quoted_text: If your Army Faction is AELDARI, at the start of the battle, make a Strands of Fate roll by rolling six D6. If you wish, you can then re-roll all of these dice, but if you do, roll one less D6. You can continue re-rolling all of the dice in this manner, rolling one less D6 each time you do, until you are satisfied with the results rolled (or until you only have a single D6 remaining). When you are satisfied with the results rolled, those remaining dice become your Fate dice for the battle. These results cannot be changed or re-rolled further, unless a rule specifically states otherwise. Keep your Fate dice to one side – this is your Fate dice pool. Once per phase, before making a dice roll for a model or unit from your army with the Strands of Fate ability, if you have one or more dice in your Fate dice pool, you can use one of those Fate dice. To do so, select one of those Fate dice to substitute that dice roll. The dice that is being substituted is not rolled; instead, the value of the selected Fate dice is used as if it had been rolled (this counts as an unmodified dice roll of that value for all rules purposes). Each Fate dice can only be used in this way once. After using a Fate dice, remove it from your Fate dice pool and roll all remaining dice that are part of that dice roll (if any).
simulator.strands_of_fate.trigger: ANY d6 roll made for a model or unit from your army with the Strands of Fate ability (not limited to a fixed list of roll types) — but capped at ONE substitution per phase for the WHOLE ARMY from the single shared Fate dice pool. Pool is generated once at the start of the battle (a reroll-down-in-size mechanic the simulator does not model — see effect). SwegHammer only wires four of the possible roll types: Advance, Charge, Hit, and Save.
simulator.strands_of_fate.effect: (approximation, two layers) Layer 1 (pool generation, unchanged by this fix): Army.fate_dice is populated with a flat 6D6 at battle start; the codex's optional reroll-all-and-shrink-the-pool mechanic (reroll down to as few as 1 die) is not modelled — SwegHammer always starts with 6. Layer 2 (spend budget, THIS fix, gate SWEG_AELDARI_FATE_FAITHFUL, default OFF): the real rule is a single ONCE-PER-PHASE, ARMY-WIDE cap — one substitution per phase from the one shared pool, for any roll of any of the four wired types. Default (gate OFF, legacy, unchanged): each of the four roll-type budgets (fate_advance / fate_charge / fate_hit / fate_save) is tracked PER SQUAD via Army._unit_budget_used, reset each battle round — this is a KNOWN OVER-COUNT versus the codex (up to ~36-40 spends/round for a 9-10-squad army, since every squad gets its own budget for every roll type every round) that predates this fix and is being left in place as the default pending screening. Gate ON: `Army.fate_budget_key` collapses the key for all four effects to one army-wide sentinel, so `mark_unit_budget`/`unit_budget_available` enforce at most ONE spend per roll-type per round army-wide (<= 4 spends/round total) — a documented APPROXIMATION of the true once-per-phase-for-any-roll cap (the four wired roll-types stand in for the four phase contexts a Fate die is actually spent in: Movement, Charge, Shooting/Fight-hit, Shooting/Fight-save), not a literal re-implementation of "once per phase" across all four simultaneously. The greedy spend heuristic (pop the lowest qualifying die that flips fail->success) and the 6-die pool are untouched by this fix; only the budget SCOPE (per-squad vs army-wide) changes. Byte-identical off.
